notes: Two-year (4 cropping cycles, 2012-2014) split-plot trial on a Vertisol at the University of Ghana research station SIREC, Kpong: biochar 0 vs 10 t/ha (main plot, applied once) x N 0/45/90/120 kg/ha (subplot), 3 replicates, irrigated lowland rice cv KRC Baika. cost_return: Gross Margin (Figure 5, 16 rows) and Value Cost Ratio (Figure 6, 12 rows), each Biochar vs Conventional at the same N rate, per cycle; values read from the vector bar charts (no data labels; no table of economic results in the PDF). Not extracted: gross returns (GR = yield x price - (variable + fixed cost)) are only in Supplementary Table S2, which is not in this PDF; the text ranges (GM increase due to biochar 132-351 US$/ha across N rates; GM increase over the control 516-1036 US$/ha with biochar vs 324-718 US$/ha with sole fertiliser; biochar VCRs 19-43% lower in cycle 1 and 6-83% higher in cycles 2-4) are ranges, not extracted. Table 1 (unit production costs per cycle: labour operations, inputs, fertiliser prices, ploughing, harvesting, land rent; rice price 430 US$/t) gives cost items, not treatment-level totals, so no rows. N-rate contrasts (N vs 0 N within an arm) are plain fertiliser rate increases, not a vocabulary practice (nutrient_mgmt_b excludes rate increases against zero), so not extracted; biochar+N against the 0 N/no-biochar control is printed only as a range, so not extracted. adoption and carbon were not extracted this round (the paper reports SOC stocks but no carbon income and no adoption data).

cost_return.site: Kpong (University of Ghana Soil and Irrigation Research Centre, SIREC)
cost_return.locator: Figure 5, panel "Cropping cycle 1, 2012", bars "Biochar" vs "Conventional", "0 kgN ha-1"
cost_return.quote: Figure 5. Gross margins (GM) of biochar (10 t·ha−1) and nitrogen fertilizer (kg·ha−1) used in irrigated rice over 4 cropping cycles (2012–2014) at Kpong, Ghana. | GM (UD$ ha-1) | Error bars are standard deviations of the means.
cost_return.note: Value read off the bar chart: the figure is vector graphics in the PDF, so bar tops and error-bar caps were measured from the drawing coordinates against the axis ticks and rounded (to 10 US$/ha); nothing computed from other data. Biochar (rice husk, 10 t/ha) was applied once, at the start of cycle 1; later cycles are its residual effect. Season: July to November 2012; the figure panel is labelled 'Cropping cycle 1, 2012'; year coded by start year (two cycles start in each of 2012 and 2013, so the panel year is not the code year for cycles 2 and 4). Both arms received the same N rate (half as NPK 15:15:15 two weeks after transplanting, half as urea at five weeks). GM subtracts only the variable costs (fertilizer, biochar, and labour for applying them: 21 US$/ha each, Table 1), i.e. the costs that vary between treatments, so budget_type = partial; seed, herbicide, irrigation water and labour, land rent, ploughing and mechanised harvesting are 'fixed costs' not subtracted in GM. Biochar cost = labour conveying the feedstock and preparing it + retort kiln rental (Table 1: 17 US$/tonne preparation), so input_production = Yes (feedstock conveyance sits inside this; not marked as transport). labour_valued = yes: all labour operations are costed per ha; the paper does not distinguish family from hired labour. Axis label prints 'UD$' (typo for US$). Rice price 430 US$/tonne (MoFA records); costs from the study site. 0 kg N arms: biochar is the only difference. The biochar cost falls in cycle 1, when biochar was applied (p18: 'higher production cost associated with applying biochar in the 1st cropping cycle').
